capability.summary: Set how widely a published version is exposed in the tenant catalog
capability.description: Implemented catalog visibility. The level is tenant (whole organization), units (only the named units, matched against the caller's token groups), applications (only the named caller applications) or hidden (default: only exact grant discovery and management views). Changing the level requires capabilities.publish, or capabilities.write plus ownership of the provider application, an exact If-Match, existing confirmed units and same-tenant applications in the designation list. Tenant and hidden levels clear both designation lists. The change is audited as capability.visibility_changed. See CAPABILITIES.md.

Implemented. Read-only view of direct cross-application trust: applications as nodes and grants as edges, with the effective state (pending, active, expired, revoked) and expiry. An administrator with trust.approve or a read-only viewer with audit.read sees every grant of its tenant; a writer with trust.write sees only grants whose provider application it owns. readOnly is true when the caller holds neither trust.write nor trust.approve. No query parameters: the tenant and scope come from the verified caller. At most 500 newest edges are returned; truncated reports more. See CAPABILITY_DIRECT_TRUST.md.

capability.summary: Accept one guarded pinned capability execution
capability.description: Opt-in guarded execution. C4B accepts only target and input and pins a published caller-owned composition. Every step rechecks original OIDC authority, active apps and independent same-tenant direct invoke grants; providers authenticate and redeem single-use step-bound tickets. C4B replay returns the durable reservation and never restores a lost lease or retries ambiguous work. Results require original consumer/subject/client and current authority. Success requires validated final output and confirmed Flowable history. No cancellation, resume, delegation or automatic retries. C4A retains its documented untouched-work replay contract. See CAPABILITY_COMPOSITION.md and CAPABILITY_EXECUTION.md. An optional context with purpose, dataSubject and dataSubjectKind declares why the call is made and whose data it concerns; it is bound into the idempotent request, sealed into the audit chain, passed to the provider on ticket redemption and listed for the data subject by GET /v1/me/data-access. When a backend invocation names a dataSubject, it needs an app consent for the capability and purpose. Emergency access remains available for backend invocations with a justification and is subject to the review backlog limit. To invoke a single capability with an exchanged bearer, Core checks the verified unit assignment and the app's direct invoke grant. A named data subject must use its canonical identifier and a matching unit consent. A missing unit grant returns 403 consent_missing. Revoked or expired grants return consent_revoked or consent_expired. A hidden subject or capability returns 404 not_found.

app=self selects only events of the verified app. Otherwise a caller with the verified regulator role sees application events for assigned units, with actor, subjectId, resourceRef, purpose and meta withheld for restricted events. A management principal with audit.read can see tenant platform audit items and the structural projection of app events. The actor filter matches the stored login or service actor. Management can match platform actors and filter app metadata by unit within the tenant. Regulators can match actors on standard events in their assigned units. The app self view can match its own actors. subjectId filtering remains unavailable in the management view. Results are ordered by occurredAt and eventId descending. Keep scope and filters unchanged with nextCursor. Existing management clients may use since and until and keep the same platform item fields. The action filter matches the event field on platform items.

capability.description: An active registered app sends only the declared event fields. Core resolves the actor from the app credential or a verified delegated user context bound to the app, stamps the app, unit when verified, and time, and appends to the tenant hash chain. subjectId is supplied only when the event concerns that subject. Use opaque references, coded purpose and non-sensitive meta. An identical retry replays the original 201 receipt. A changed request with the same key returns 422 idempotency_key_reused. Up to 120 new entries per app per minute.

headerParameters.name: Idempotency-Key
headerParameters.description: Required UUID for this write. A missing or malformed key returns 400 invalid_request. Core retains the first recorded result for 24 hours, scoped to the verified tenant and caller, HTTP method and concrete request path. Within that window, the same key and logical request replay the first status, body and resource headers without another write. A changed body or write precondition for the same key returns 422 idempotency_key_reused. Concurrent identical requests share one result; every replay requires current authorization.

capability.description: app=self selects only events of the verified app. Otherwise a caller with the verified regulator role sees application events for assigned units, with actor, subjectId, resourceRef, purpose and meta withheld for restricted events. A management principal with audit.read can see tenant platform audit items and the structural projection of app events. The actor filter matches the stored login or service actor. Management can match platform actors and filter app metadata by unit within the tenant. Regulators can match actors on standard events in their assigned units. The app self view can match its own actors. subjectId filtering remains unavailable in the management view. Export a consistent snapshot up to the tenant chain head. Each tenant can open two snapshots at a time. An export matching more than 10,000 events fails with 400 audit_export_too_large; narrow the time range and retry. The first line identifies the head even for an empty result. An empty tenant chain has sequence 0 and the zero hash of 64 zeros, which the chain verifier also accepts as the genesis predecessor. Event lines carry their chain sequence and stored digest for reconciliation. Scoped exports can have gaps and redacted fields; verify the full tenant chain through the existing privileged verify endpoint.

capability.summary: Seal pending audit events and verify the tenant hash chain
capability.description: Implemented. Seals the caller tenant's pending audit events into a SHA-256 hash chain, then recomputes every sealed entry. A modified, deleted or reordered sealed event, or a removed newest entry, is reported in firstBreak; nothing is sealed on top of a broken chain. Requires a verified management principal with audit.read in its own tenant. The database administrator remains trusted; see AUDIT.md.

capability.summary: List the caller tenant's enrolled management principals
capability.description: Implemented. Returns up to 1000 enrolled principals of the caller's tenant and issuer with subject, issuer, managementClient, permissions, enabled, and the optional presentation profile displayName, organization, jobTitle and kind (admin or application), each null when unset. Never returns secrets, tokens or request bodies and never calls the identity provider's admin API. Requires a verified management principal with audit.read in its own tenant; the database function enforces the tenant, issuer and permission. No query parameters.

capability.summary: Read the tenant/application tree with current trust relations
capability.description: Implemented. Builds a read-only tree from real data: the root is the caller tenant (kind platform), children are the applications registered in that tenant (kind application), and relations are non-revoked, unexpired direct trust grants between those applications. Relation labels are the real published capability title, falling back to the exact capabilityId. There is no separate organization table, so applications appear directly under the tenant. At most 1000 applications and 500 relations; truncated reports more. Requires a verified management principal with audit.read in its own tenant. No query parameters.

capability.summary: Read one-minute traffic buckets for the recent window
capability.description: Implemented. Returns exactly minutes chronological one-minute buckets ending with the current minute, including empty minutes as zeroes, with requests, 4xx/5xx errors, average latency and maximum latency, plus totals for the window. Counters are real observations recorded as responses finish. They live in the Core process only, are per instance and reset when Core restarts; no database or persistence is involved. Metrics requests are counted like any other request. A verified management principal with audit.read is required. Query parameters are closed; unknown, repeated or malformed values return 400.

queryParameters.name: minutes
queryParameters.description: Number of one-minute buckets ending with the current minute.

capability.summary: Read the newest requests observed by Core
capability.description: Implemented. Returns up to limit of the newest requests, newest first. Each entry contains only the observation time, method, normalized path, status and duration. Query strings, fragments, headers, bodies, tokens, subjects and recognizable UUID/token path segments are never retained. The in-memory ring holds at most the newest 200 requests; it is per Core process and resets when Core restarts. A verified management principal with audit.read is required. Query parameters are closed; unknown, repeated or malformed values return 400.

queryParameters.name: limit
queryParameters.description: Maximum number of newest requests to return.

capability.summary: List the data subject's visible access events
capability.description: Use the verified token subjectId, tenant and issuer; a supplied subject identifier never selects another person. A missing verified claim returns 403. Merge capability calls and application events declared visible to this data subject at append time. Order by accessedAt descending and accessId descending. Use accessId for flagging either source. Preserve entries, generatedAt and truncated; truncated is true when nextCursor is present.

capability.summary: Flag an access event for review
capability.description: Use the verified token subjectId, tenant and issuer; a supplied subject identifier never selects another person. A missing verified claim returns 403. Applies to either visible source. Store a separate report. Retrying the same reason returns the original report; attempting to change it returns 409. Nonvisible entries return 404.

Return the latest 200 consents belonging to the data subject. Uses the authenticated login, tenant and issuer for compatibility. A supplied subjectId claim must match the operator binding or the request returns 403.

capability.summary: Grant consent as the data subject
capability.description: Grant the declared purposes for an existing capability, expiring within 366 days. Provide either consumerAppId for an active app or recipientUnit for a confirmed unit in the same tenant. A unit grant requires an operator-bound subjectId from the subject login. App grants keep their existing scope.

headerParameters.name: Idempotency-Key
headerParameters.description: Required UUID for this write. A missing or malformed key returns 400 invalid_request. Core retains the first recorded result for 24 hours, scoped to the verified tenant and caller, HTTP method and concrete request path. Within that window, the same key and logical request replay the first status, body and resource headers without another write. A changed body or write precondition for the same key returns 422 idempotency_key_reused. Concurrent identical requests share one result; every replay requires current authorization.

capability.description: Revoking an already revoked consent returns its current representation. Uses the authenticated login, tenant and issuer for compatibility. A supplied subjectId claim must match the operator binding or the request returns 403.

capability.summary: Submit feedback on the subject's own break-glass access
capability.description: Use the verified token subjectId, tenant and issuer; a supplied subject identifier never selects another person. A missing verified claim returns 403. Use the execution ID from the break-glass access entry. Feedback is separate from the management review and the original audit event. Identical retries return the saved receipt; different feedback after submission conflicts. Keep personal content out of message.

capability.summary: Read aggregate record and file counts for the caller tenant
capability.description: Implemented. Returns per-application structured record counts by collection plus aggregate file count, bytes, quarantine count and last modification time, and tenant totals. Requires a verified management principal with audit.read in its own tenant; the database function and private role enforce tenant scope. Record content, object keys, file names and bytes are never returned. Object metadata is reduced from the object filer; if the filer is not configured files is null for every application, and if it is configured but unavailable the request fails closed. No query parameters.

capability.summary: Browse one directory level of an application's object store
capability.description: Implemented. Returns exactly one level of the application's private file tree: folders with aggregate file count, bytes and latest modification time, and files with a partially masked name, extension, size, scan status and modification time. Requires a verified management principal with audit.read in its own tenant; the storage summary function and private role enforce the permission. The path defaults to the root, is canonicalised, rejects traversal, control characters and segments longer than 255 characters, and is limited to 512 characters. Object keys, internal filer paths, versions and bytes are never returned. The object filer must be configured; if it is unavailable the request fails closed.

queryParameters.name: application
queryParameters.description: Application whose private file tree is listed.

queryParameters.name: path
queryParameters.description: Folder path relative to the application root; defaults to the root.

capability.summary: Read the inferred field structure of an application's collections
capability.description: Implemented. Returns each collection owned by the application with its record count, latest update time and the field names inferred from at most the 200 newest records. Field types are string, number, boolean, object, array, mixed or null; fillRate is the percentage of sampled records where the field is present and not null. Requires a verified management principal with audit.read in its own tenant; the new migration-026 function and private role enforce permission and tenant scope. Record values, sample rows, object keys and bytes are never returned.

queryParameters.name: application
queryParameters.description: Application whose collection structure is read.

capability.summary: List the caller tenant workflow executions, newest first
capability.description: Implemented. Returns a bounded page of Flowable history scoped to the caller tenant. Requires a verified management principal with audit.read in its own tenant; the private workflow audit role enforces the permission. Running rows include the active task name, assignee and candidate groups. The title is the workflow definition name, followed by input.reference only when that value is a string matching ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9-]{0,31}$; without a definition name it is null. No other input fields contribute; personal names, other identifiers, record content and workflow variables are never included. The internal junctura_c4a_single definition is excluded.

capability.summary: Read per-feature call counts for the recent window
capability.description: Implemented. Groups the same real, in-memory one-minute observations as getTrafficMetrics by product feature (data, files, workflows, approvals, sharing, capabilities, applications, consents, secrets, audit, other), derived from the normalized request path. Each feature carries requests, 4xx/5xx errors, average and maximum latency and a per-minute request series, sorted by requests descending. Counters live in the Core process only, are per instance and reset when Core restarts. A verified management principal with audit.read is required. Query parameters are closed; unknown, repeated or malformed values return 400.

queryParameters.name: minutes
queryParameters.description: Number of one-minute buckets ending with the current minute.

capability.summary: Read the read-only workflow dashboard for the caller tenant
capability.description: Implemented. Returns every business workflow definition with its owning product, ordered steps with responsible parties, and counts of running, completed and cancelled executions, plus totals. It is a read-only aggregate: it never starts, completes or cancels anything and never reads workflow variables or personal data. Technical definitions used only for Core verification are excluded. Requires a verified management principal with audit.read in its own tenant. The query string must be empty.
